Subject: NimHealth onboarding: inference performance sprint charter

Hi Sana / Tom —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. As discussed in last week's call, we want to run a focused implementation sprint to get NimHealth onto a cost-optimized inference configuration that meets your 95th percentile latency target (sub-400ms per request) while minimizing token cost.

Proposed high-level approach (short):
- Week 0 (prep): collect traffic profile, example prompts, and current request/response sizes (attached: nimhealth-map-v1.xlsx)
- Week 1: batching and KV/cache policies + baseline metrics
- Week 2: quantization profile evaluation + perf/cost tradeoffs
- Week 3: routing/rollout and canary to production

Key asks from NimHealth for kickoff:
1) Representative prompt set and a small request sample (1–2k requests) or a replay window
2) Latency SLOs by route and peak traffic hours
3) Any regulatory constraints that affect private deployment or model variants

I attached a quick mapping sheet (nimhealth-map-v1.xlsx). I can convert this into a one-page sprint charter if that helps. Proposed kickoff: Tue Mar 29, 10:00am PT (30–45m).

If that sounds good, I’ll circulate a charter and assign owners.

—Sean

Attached is a concise sprint charter (rdw-sprint-charter-v1.pdf) — TL;DR below and includes explicit owners and deliverables:

Sprint charter (3 weeks):
- Objective: Reduce per-token cost by 25% vs FP16 baseline while preserving p95 latency <= 400ms on main route.
- Deliverables:
  * Baseline report (latency, cost per 1k tokens, req distribution) — owner: Monica
  * Batching & caching config with A/B canary — owner: Karthik
  * Quantization benchmark matrix (fp16, int8, awq_q4_0) — owner: Redwood Research (cc'd: Karthik)
  * Routing policy plan (primary hosted -> fallback to ded. pool when latency > 500ms or concurrency spike) — owner: Sean
- Success criteria: validated quant profile with <3% quality regression on 200 eval prompts and cost reduction >= 20%
- Meetings: kickoff (Mar 29), mid-sprint check (Week 2), final sign-off (Week 3)

Operational notes / escalation:
- Primary on-call: Monica (implementation), backup: Karthik. For exec-level escalations call Sean directly. We will publish a short 1-page escalation playbook after kickoff.

Kickoff options: Tue Mar 29 10:00am PT or Wed Mar 30 9:00am PT. Please confirm.

Sean / team — adding a quick technical checklist to make the sprint more runnable and to reduce back-and-forth during Week 1: 

Technical checklist (suggested, actionable):
- Data & traffic: place anonymized 2k sample into shared Drive folder (Sana — thanks). We’ll run a small replay harness against hosted test env.
- Batching: start with dynamic batching with max_batch_size=64 and target_latency_goal=200ms; we will iterate the max_batch_size based on p95 observations.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix/cache for repeated context (TTL=60s initially); we’ll measure cache hit rate and adjust.
- Quantization: run fp16 baseline, then AWQ Q4_0 and INT8 quant. Prioritize AWQ Q4_0 for small quality delta and bigger performance wins on CPU-backed fallback.
- Routing: config two policies — (A) latency-first for clinical route (prefer low-latency GPUs), (B) cost-first for batch analytics (route to ded. lower-cost pool). We'll instrument a fallback to an FP16 variant if quantized model fails quality checks.
- Eval & quality gating: we will use a 200-prompt eval set from NimHealth; quality regression allowed <=3% on task-specific metrics.

I’ll prepare a small ops snippet and a config sample to drop into your repo this week. Monica / Laura — I’ll need a quick sync to confirm access to nimhealth's test key and S3 bucket.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
